_about.what: THE ROOT MAP (LGIC_BLANKFIX contract C-REGISTRY, outcome FWD-7; Andrew-direct 2026-09-21 'b': the resource-to-system lookup is compiled from a small handwritten Terraform-root map, with only genuine exceptions handwritten). One entry per Terraform root under infra/aws/terraform/: the default system, scope and source of the names that root declares, plus its exceptions. Read by lib/opal_naming_rootmap.py load_map() and by nothing else at this write: grade() does not read this file yet, so an entry changes no verdict and no generated view.
_about.row_fields: roots.<root folder name>: system (a systems.json key, the default owner of the root's names); scope (a scopes.json scope); source (a systems.json key); evidence (what was read to decide the three); exceptions (a list of {name, type, system, evidence}, unique per (name, type) within the root).
_about.authority: Written by 4.0.0_SA_CRO, the registry's owner, from the proposal of 0.9.0_WK_LGIC_BLANKFIX~3 (org/missions/D14/LGIC/LGIC_BLANKFIX/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_LGIC_BLANKFIX~3/ROOT_MAP_PROPOSED.json @8910a3de90), asked by 2.0.0_SA_COO~G msg 106217. The roots object is that proposal's, unchanged.
_about.not_decided: bd-pipeline: the default system is a DECISION only for names that resources.json already places (57 of 57 reproduced at this write). Twelve declarations (ten distinct names) of inline IAM policies in that root carry a {system} blank and have no row and no exception: s3-etf-ownership, cloudwatch-metrics, pipeline-chain (iam.tf:256 and :614), s3-access (iam.tf:363 and :855), runner-shared-read, AdditionalPermissions, gold-layer-trigger, events-emit, cloudfront-invalidate, invoke-price-update. The default does NOT decide them. Two reasons: (1) an inline policy follows its role, and s3-access at iam.tf:855 sits on the blackdiamond allocation-processor role, which the default would call advi (row LGIC_BLANKFIX-W3-S1: the (name, type) key cannot tell the two s3-access policies apart); (2) Andrew's ruling 3 and CALL 3 of 2026-09-21 say an AWS-service-led or inline policy name is not asked for a system at all, which is LGIC_BLANKFIX's fourth verdict (C-VERDICT), not a map entry. A compiler that reads this file must not emit a system for those twelve from the default.

bd-pipeline.evidence: Read: every .tf under infra/aws/terraform/bd-pipeline/ (96 graded names by lib/opal_naming.py census_tf_names), every folder under infra/aws/lambda/bd-pipeline/ (43 repository-plane names by census_repo), and the 57 names of this root that infra/logic/registry/resources.json already places. FIRM: every Lambda and box reads and writes the bucket opal-data-bd (scopes.json alias of 49financial) and the secret blackdiamond/49f/session, so scope = 49financial. SOURCE: the ingest side (bd-49f-runner, bd-49f-fees-runner, bd-49f-session-trigger, bd-allocations/transactions/fees/assets boxes) pulls one vendor's feed, Black Diamond, so source = blackdiamond (the SECRET blackdiamond/49f/session is already CONFORMANT). SYSTEM DEFAULT: advi -- 31 of the 57 placed names are rows resolved as 'PRODUCT (ROOT)' (the gold layer, step functions, shared exporter and trigger roles, canonical prices: SY1 second clause, feeds combined into the product); the 26 rows that differ are carried as exceptions below with each row's own evidence (16 blackdiamond 'INTEGRATION (CODE)' rows, marketdata 4, globgrph 2, schwab, cloudops, firmsep, tradeops 1 each). The 12 names with a {system} blank and no row are NOT exceptions: they resolve to the default here and are listed to the issuer as not decided by SY1 on repository evidence.
